Hi Sara — thanks for the RFP and the clear ask. Quick read-through attached a short one-pager with two starter constructs and a note on partner routing. High level summary here so procurement has something to review quickly: 

Option A — Flat annual subscription (recommended for predictable budgeting)
- Single list price that covers up to X usage (we'd set X ~6B tokens/year initially)
- Annual prepay; automatic annual renewal at market index with opt-out window
- Reseller margin: represented on AWS as a 18% reseller pass-through (invoice routing) or as a seller credit depending on partner preference
- Onboarding credit: one-time $30,000 credit applied to first invoice OR applied as a line-item credit in the private-offer configuration

Option B — Modular/tiered per-token (recommended for elasticity)
- Base per-100M-token price with tiered discounts at 2.5B, 5B, 8B thresholds
- Usage billing monthly; can pair with minimum monthly commitment to get steeper rates
- Reseller margin: typically 15–20% (we can standardize at 18% in the private offer metadata)
- Onboarding credit: can be applied as first-month invoice offset or as a pre-funded commitment buy-down

Docs: we can provide SOC 2 Type II report, data retention notes, and a short KMS integration summary. I attached the one-pager and our private-offer template for AWS to show mechanics.

Next steps: if procurement prefers flat for the first year, we'll draft the private offer with the onboarding credit as a line-item. If they prefer modular, we'll propose a monthly billing cadence and a 6–12 month minimum commit to secure the lower tiers. Which direction should we prepare to prototype?

Thanks,

Subject: Fwd: EDU RFP — margin and ops implications

Looping internal ops + finance for margin impact and how we'll encode the rebate. Quick notes: 

- If we route the reseller margin via marketplace invoice pass-through, partner (EduPartners) receives their share directly and our revenue recognition is cleaner but invoicing and tax flows require partner onboarding in our billing system. Ops time: ~3 business days to set routing.
- If we represent margin as a seller credit, Redwood pays the partner out of our invoice balance; easier for partner but increases our short-term cash impact and requires mapping credits in accounting (longer reconciliation).
- Onboarding credit: $30k is reasonable but we should offer two forms: credit note (applied after invoice as a refund) or upfront reduction (line-item in private offer). Finance prefers line-item for simplicity; partner often prefers credit note to keep ledger neutral.

Recommendation: propose Option B (modular) to the customer with a standardized 18% reseller margin routed via invoice pass-through. Offer $30k onboarding credit as a line-item in the private offer but include an option to convert to credit note if procurement demands.

Related links: HubSpot deal and internal private-offer playbook attached.

-Camila

Hi Sara / Procurement team — following internal ops alignment, here's a concise draft proposal for the procurement review. I've attached the one-pager with scenario math and a filled private-offer template to show how credits and reseller routing appear on AWS.

Proposal (draft):
- Pricing construct: Modular per-100M tokens, with the following tiered list price (example):
  - 0–2.5B tokens/year: $120 per 100M tokens
  - 2.5B–5B tokens/year: $105 per 100M tokens
  - 5B–8B tokens/year: $90 per 100M tokens
  - 8B+ tokens/year: $78 per 100M tokens
- Commit: 12-month initial term with monthly usage billing; option for annual prepay at a 5% discount
- Reseller margin: 18% routed via AWS invoice pass-through (EduPartners invoice mapping) — this preserves clean settlements and ensures partner sees line-item revenue
- Onboarding credit: $30,000 applied as a line-item reduction on the first invoice (we can alternatively issue a credit note post-invoice per procurement preference)
- Docs we will provide: SOC 2 Type II, data handling FAQ, KMS integration summary, and sample MSA

Next steps: if this looks aligned, can we schedule a 30 minute procurement + legal sync next week? Suggested times: Mon 12/20 14:00–15:00 PT or Tue 12/21 09:00–09:30 PT.

Thanks all — I copied Rajiv at EduPartners so he can confirm the routing approach.
